fns.desc: In wpas_sd_req_asp, for a prefix ('*'-suffixed) ASP service-name query, the length-mismatch guard at line 600 is skipped (`!prefix && ...`), so `os_memcmp(adv_data->svc_name, svc, svc_len)` at line 604 compares `svc_len` bytes (attacker-controlled, up to 254, from wire-derived P2P SD request query[0]) against `adv_data->svc_name`, a locally-registered heap string that may be shorter than svc_len — a genuine out-of-bounds heap read past the end of svc_name's allocation whenever a peer sends a prefix search longer than a registered service name.

In wpas_sd_req_upnp, the 2-byte length placeholder (`len_pos`) and protocol/trans-id bytes are already committed to `resp` (lines 424-426) before the `os_malloc(query_len)` at line 429; if that allocation fails, the function returns without ever writing the status/response bytes or filling in `len_pos` via WPA_PUT_LE16, leaving a malformed/uninitialized-length TLV committed into the shared aggregate SD response buffer. Low severity (OOM-triggered only), no memory corruption, but a real protocol-correctness/uninitialized-data-exposure defect on the error path.
